content: I replaced the M3x6r screw with one of the old screws from the heatbed assembly. These are shorter and seem to be more than tight enough.

Someone mentioned it already, but just to reiterate, I would highly recommend you pre-thread the hole in the printed part with the M3x6r screw before final assembly. Go slow. A turn or two, then back it out. Rinse and repeat until the head of the screw is about 2mm from the face of the hole and you should have a much easier time installing the expansion joint without the part splitting along the layer lines adjacent to the hole.
I cannot for the life of me get this to any tightness with the tools I have.

see my comment at step 21 for  this.  the hole in the expansion joint has threads on it and can bind with the allen key.  i used a very thin flat blade screwdriver that the tip was wide enough to engage the M3x6r slots but thinner than the expansion joint hole to tighten without splitting...
Yep +1. Very little pressure, and it split

I was running the screw down and the part split when the screw was only run in about halfway. Evidently I should've slowed down. Still seems usable but I'm hoping Prusa posts files so I can print a replacement.

replies.content: Thanks for the warning. I found screwing in a little then backing off like using a tap and die set worked well and didn't split.
Thanks, this method worked well. Tighten, loosen. Tighten a bit more, loosen, etc. Took a while, but didn't have problems.
